title: Control Over MAS on Choice of Monetary Regime or Total Level of Reserves Held
what_it_is: Control Over MAS on Choice of Monetary Regime or Total Level of Reserves Held

sections.label: MAS monetary policy autonomy
sections.summary: MAS has full autonomy over choosing monetary policy instruments and formulating monetary policy within its stated mandate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Within this stated mandate, MAS has full autonomy over the appropriate choice of monetary policy instrument and the formulation of monetary policy.

sections.label: MAS official foreign reserves assessment
sections.summary: MAS assesses needed OFR for monetary policy, referencing internationally accepted reserve adequacy measures and Singapore's open economy and financial markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS assesses how much OFR is needed for the purpose of implementing its monetary policy, taking reference from internationally accepted measures of reserve adequacy as well as the highly open nature of our economy and financial markets.

sections.label: MAS independence within Government
sections.summary: MAS lacks statutory independence but is independent within the Government, operating autonomously without interference, while coordinating with other agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The MAS' model is different – MAS may not have statutory independence in the way that many central banks do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: It is not independent of the Government, but it is independent within the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS operates with considerable autonomy, with no interference from the rest of the Government, be it in the conduct of monetary policy or supervisory policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Yet, MAS is part of the broader Singapore Public Service, working closely with other Government agencies for the national benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And macro-prudential policies are successful in Singapore only because the MAS, the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of National Development coordinate and use their respective policy tools in a concerted manner.

sections.label: Singapore's distinct circumstances
sections.summary: Singapore acts on its own because its circumstances differ from other jurisdictions, being a financial centre, small place and very open economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, we do things in our own because our circumstances are very different from many other jurisdictions around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We play an outsized role in global financial markets, for example, as a financial centre; and we are also a very small place but a very open economy.
